svg.aria-label: Four pictures of Python names pointing to list objects: b = a shares one list, a.copy() makes a new one, a shallow copy shares the inner lists, and a mutable default argument is shared by every call

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Names point to objects: where mutability bites

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A name is a label on an object. b = a adds a second label; it does not copy the list.
b = a # b refers to the SAME list

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: b = a: two names, one list

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Not a copy, just a second name for the same object.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: b = a.copy() # or a[:] or list(a)

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Two list objects: changing b leaves a as it was.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: a.copy() is shallow: inner lists are shared

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Outer list new, inner lists shared. copy.deepcopy(a) is truly independent.

svg.text: Mutable default: one list for every call
